questions.q: At Meridian Outfitters, why does Private make sense as the OWD for Account, Contact, and Opportunity?
options: Reps' territories don't overlap, so there's no default reason for one rep to see another's accounts
Private is always the correct default for every org
Private is required before you can create a role hierarchy
Private is the only OWD that supports permission sets
questions.explain: The OWD choice follows the business shape: non-overlapping territories mean no default reason to share, so Private fits.

questions.q: With Private OWD and a role hierarchy that mirrors the org chart, how does a Regional Sales Manager see their reps' opportunities without a sharing rule?
options: They don't — a sharing rule is always required
The manager must be manually added to each opportunity's sharing
Visibility rolls up the role hierarchy automatically from Private OWD
Managers get access only through permission sets
questions.explain: Role-hierarchy rollup is the mechanism: Private OWD plus a hierarchy gives managers automatic visibility into their reports' records.

questions.q: Why does Sales Operations get a role-hierarchy sharing rule instead of being placed in the sales role hierarchy?
options: Sharing rules are always preferred over hierarchy
Role hierarchies can't grant read-only access
Permission sets can't be combined with roles
Sales Operations supports every region and isn't part of one chain of command
questions.explain: Sales Ops's access doesn't follow a single reporting chain, which is exactly the situation a sharing rule — not hierarchy placement — is built for.

questions.q: Why is a criteria-based sharing rule used for national accounts rather than relying on hierarchy?
options: Criteria-based rules are faster to build than hierarchy
National accounts are co-sold across regions, which the hierarchy's chain-of-command shape can't reach
Criteria-based rules replace the need for OWDs
Hierarchy only works for Leads, not Opportunities
questions.explain: National accounts cross regional boundaries, so a criteria-based rule (Account Type = National Account) reaches the co-sell team that hierarchy alone can't.

questions.q: What's the risk the lesson calls out in choosing Public Read/Write just to avoid building sharing rules?
options: It trades a little setup time now for a data model where nothing is actually private
It has no downside — it's always the simpler choice
Public Read/Write is not a valid OWD option
It automatically disables the role hierarchy
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a real tradeoff: the convenience of skipping sharing-rule work costs genuine data privacy across the org.
